source_text: Sic egi hactenus, quasi vim donorum et vulnerum, in contrariis licet effectibus, aequalem tamen Apostolus aestimasset; crescit autem dubio procul sublimitas sanae fidei quam tuemur, cum consideratur Paulus non solum remediis gratiae aegritudinem non praetulisse culparum, verum etiam copiosiora beneficia iudicasse dispendiis.
pass_a_gloss: So I have acted until now, as if the Apostle had estimated the force of gifts and of wounds, although in contrary effects, nevertheless equal; but the sublimity of the sound faith which we guard grows beyond doubt, when it is considered that Paul not only did not prefer the sickness of faults to the remedies of grace, but even judged the benefits more copious than the losses.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS vulnus; Blaise sin as wound

pass_b_english: So far I have argued as though the apostle regarded the power of the gifts and the wounds as equal, although opposite in effect. But the sound faith we defend undoubtedly rises still higher when we consider that Paul not only did not rank the sickness of sins above the remedies of grace: he judged the benefits more abundant than the losses (compare Romans 5:15) (Romans 5:15).

choices.why: In this book Julian usually means the Savior's gift abounding against Adam's sin (Rom 5), not later system-grace as a substance, and not 'favoritism' unless a suum-cuique definition is in play.
Julian's pair with iustitia: guilt as culpable will, not a nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
